mark_split.label: Apply the property with a = π/2

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.69 — SAQ chapter 10 'Definite Integrals', answer 84, on a printed Super Scoring Page (SSP 69). Printed appearance: AP 19, 17. No margin mark tags are printed for this item, so the 1+1+2 split is OURS, patterned on the identical shape carried by the two printed splits immediately before it in this chapter (answers 82 and 83, both 1+1+2). BOOK ERROR, corrected here: the printed working's second line (the x → π/2−x form) repeats the FIRST line's numerator sin⁵x unchanged instead of turning it into cos⁵x — the correct second form's numerator is cos⁵x, as re-derived below and as required for the addition step to reach 1. The book's stated final answer, π/4, is nonetheless correct (it is exactly what the corrected working also gives). Chapter star rank ★★★ applies. Boundary reading: printed p.67 (Hyperbola SAQ) and printed p.72 (Differential Equations SAQ opening) confirm the chapter span. No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 stand in for the back-test). This integral is re-answered as the first Q16 item on the Bullet Model Paper, book p.110, with the corrected working already present there — same final value π/4.

insider_note: The book prints this question's second line with an error: it repeats sin⁵x instead of turning it into cos⁵x after the substitution. Write the corrected line — cos⁵x — the wrong line would not let the addition step reach 1.

steps.label: Apply the property with a = π/2
steps.margin_note: One mark. Label the given integral (1).
steps.memory_tip: sin(π/2 − x) = cosx — always check the substituted form actually changes the base.
steps.why: Labelling the given integral (1) sets it up for comparison with the transformed second form.
common_mistakes: Not writing the property line before using it.
Skipping the label (1), which then confuses the addition step.

steps.label: Write the second form
steps.margin_note: One more mark. sin⁵x turns into cos⁵x — check this line carefully, it is easy to leave it unchanged by mistake.
steps.memory_tip: sin(π/2 − x) = cosx, so sin⁵(π/2 − x) = cos⁵x — the base swaps, the power 5 stays.
steps.why: Under x → π/2 − x, sinx becomes cosx, so sin⁵x becomes cos⁵x in the numerator, while the denominator (a sum of both powers) reappears unchanged.
common_mistakes: Leaving the numerator as sin⁵x instead of turning it into cos⁵x — a printed error in some editions of this exact question.
Forgetting that the denominator, being a sum of both terms, is unaffected by the swap.

steps.label: Add and solve
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The numerator sum equals the denominator, so the fraction is 1.
steps.memory_tip: sin⁵x + cos⁵x over sin⁵x + cos⁵x is always 1 — the whole point of the swap was to make the two numerators add up to the denominator.
steps.why: The added numerator matches the denominator exactly, so the integrand is 1 for every x, reducing the integral to the length of the interval.
common_mistakes: Adding a wrongly-copied second form and getting a numerator that does NOT match the denominator.
Forgetting to divide by 2 at the end.
